outlook.statement: The Company proposes to expand/diversify its business activities and to undertake the activities covered under the proposed new object clause.
The acquisition is expected to create long-term business opportunities, generate operational synergies and strengthen the Company's presence in this sector.

The proposed deployment of the Issue Proceeds in PSKPL will enable PSKPL to reduce its outstanding borrowings and consequent finance costs, meet the enhanced working capital requirements arising from increased crushing volumes, and augment on-site storage capacity at its existing factory through the proposed warehouse, thereby reducing dependence on third-party storage, improving inventory management and enabling better realisation. This is expected to strengthen the consolidated financial position of the Company and improve returns to the Members over the medium term.

The Company's focus is to strengthen its existing business operations and explore opportunities for future growth. The Company aims to expand its business activities, develop new commercial opportunities, and enhance its operational capabilities to achieve sustainable growth and create value for its stakeholders.
The said acquisition marks your Company's entry into the sugar manufacturing and allied agro-processing business.

The Company is at an inflexion point. Following the change in control during the year, the change of name, the realignment of the Main Objects Clause and the divestment of the erstwhile subsidiary, the Company has commenced a transition from a purely financial services facilitation model towards an integrated agro-processing and sugar business, anchored by the acquisition of Penganga Sakhar Karkhana Private Limited after the close of the year. The proposals placed before the Members at the 41st Annual General Meeting – the increase in the Authorised Share Capital, the alteration of the Main Objects Clause and the Articles of Association, the issue of Convertible Warrants on a preferential basis and the shifting of the Registered Office to Pune – are directed at providing the capital base and the corporate framework for that transition. The Company expects that the integration of the sugar business and the deployment of the proceeds of the proposed preferential issue will be the principal determinants of its performance in the coming years.

Your company strives to maintain pace with the fast development in the Indian economy, tremendous competition and latest in technology and know-how with its limited resources. Your company will try to start its activity with value addition products gradually to make its share in global market and expecting growth in the times ahead.

The Company has in place a mechanism to identify, assess, monitor and mitigate various risks to key business objectives. Major risks identified by the businesses and functions are systematically addressed through mitigating actions on a continuing basis.
The segment is characterized by thin margins, dependence on originating partners and intense competition from both established intermediaries and technology-led entrants.

The sugar industry in India is a regulated industry, subject to the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, the Fair and Remunerative Price mechanism and periodic Government directions on export quotas, ethanol blending and monthly release.

During the period under review, the Company underwent a change in its management and control. The previous management had not maintained the Structured Digital Database (SDD) in the manner prescribed under the applicable provisions of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015.

During the period under review, the Company's website was not fully maintained and updated in accordance with the requirements of Regulation 46 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

BSE Limited, while processing the request for change of name, sought certain clarifications and supporting documents in relation to compliance with Regulation 45(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The Company is in the process of addressing the observations raised by BSE Limited.

Business transition risk: The Company is entering a business in which it has no operating history. The integration of the sugar and agro-processing business, the retention of its management and workforce and the realisation of the expected synergies are subject to execution risk.

Regulatory risk: The sugar industry is a regulated industry and is materially affected by Government policy on cane pricing, export quotas, ethanol blending, monthly release mechanisms and levies. Adverse changes in such policy could affect margins. The financial services facilitation business is dependent on the regulatory framework governing business correspondents and lending service providers, and on the outsourcing policies of the Company's partner institutions.

Agri-commodity and seasonality risk: Sugarcane availability, recovery rates and sugar prices are affected by monsoon conditions, acreage, pest incidence and the crushing cycle, none of which is within the control of the Company.
Concentration and counterparty risk: The financial services facilitation business depends on a limited number of originating partners, and the loss of any material partner could affect revenue.

Financial risk: The Company has incurred a loss during the year under review and its net worth has been eroded. The Company's ability to fund the proposed expansion is contingent upon the successful completion of the proposed preferential issue.

Dilution risk: The proposed issue of up to 4,00,00,000 Convertible Warrants, if fully subscribed and converted, will expand the paid-up equity share capital from 5,00,000 Equity Shares to 4,05,00,000 Equity Shares, resulting in substantial dilution for Members who do not participate.
Human resources risk: The Company operated with a small workforce during the year and is dependent on a limited number of key personnel.
Threats include slow down of Indian economy, myths and misconceptions about minerals and its impact on environment and competition from the global market.

Due to rapid changes in the technologies, business dimensions and complexities, regulatory changes and environmental concerns, competitions from global players, fluctuation of price and technological obsolescence and various types of risks have emerged.

orders_or_contracts.statement: Pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement dated March 31, 2026, your Company transferred its entire shareholding in Exuberant Systems Private Limited to ANS Buggy LLP for a consideration of ₹4,68,24,000/- (Rupees Four Crore Sixty-Eight Lakh Twenty-Four Thousand only).
